note: Theorem 2.7 is a generic preservation result for arbitrary random variables (X >=rh Y with IRHR => X^T >=rh Y^T; X <=hr Y with DHR => X^T <=hr Y^T), proof deferred to reference [4]; fully general nonparametric class, out of scope.

Theorem 2.8 (X <=hr Y and X or Y DHR => X <=disp Y) holds for arbitrary random variables and its proof is cited to Shaked et al. [2]; a fully general nonparametric implication, not a family-specific claim.
Theorem 2.9 (X <=hr Y and X or Y DHR => X <=LU Y) is the same generic implication cited to Ebrahimi et al. [3]; out of scope as a fully general nonparametric result.

records.quote: Theorem 3.6. Let X1, ...., Xn (Y1, ...., Yn) be the set of continuous independent random variables having Xi ~ Gum(mu_i, sigma) (Yi ~ Gum(mu*_i, sigma)), i = 1, 2, ...., n. Then, if (mu_1, ..., mu_n) >=^m (mu*_1, ..., mu*_n), we have 1. X_{1:n} <=disp Y_{1:n}; 2. X_{1:n} <=LU Y_{1:n}.
records.family: Gumbel Gum(mu_i, sigma), common scale sigma, location parameters mu_i vs mu*_i
